purpose: Pre-result, falsifiable mechanistic hypotheses about what controls 120 C thermal-hold viscosity drift in the local reactive-PUR family. Registered before any V4 experiment selection and before the held-out validation outcome is loaded.

reference_observations.source: original local E1/E5 120 C thermal-hold measurements
reference_observations.note: E1 is the least-drifting original formulation and is used as the pre-result reference level. No follow-up formulation or measurement is referenced.

hypotheses.name: reactive-core / stoichiometry-only
hypotheses.statement: Thermal-hold drift is set by the reactive prepolymer core alone. Resin-like modifiers are chemically inert at hold temperature and act only as mass dilution of reaction-capable material, so the drift coefficient scales linearly with the reactive mass fraction phi_r.
hypotheses.falsified_if: matched-window drift is substantially below the linear-dilution prediction at the same reactive mass fraction, beyond measurement resolution
hypotheses.supported_if: matched-window drift agrees with E1_drift * phi_r within measurement resolution

hypotheses.name: resin-modification / superlinear suppression
hypotheses.statement: Resin modification suppresses time-dependent viscosity growth more strongly than mass dilution alone, by lowering the effective concentration and encounter frequency of reaction-capable species within a non-reactive continuum. Drift falls well below the linear-dilution prediction.
hypotheses.falsified_if: matched-window drift at a resin-modified composition remains at or above the linear-dilution prediction
hypotheses.supported_if: matched-window drift is below half the linear-dilution prediction

hypotheses.name: dual-axis modifier specialization
hypotheses.statement: The two modifier axes act on different rheological coordinates. The acrylic-like axis principally relocates the realized viscosity level, whereas the minor tackifier-like axis is required for drift suppression. Acrylic addition alone therefore does not reach the low-drift regime.
hypotheses.predicts_drift_pct: low only when the minor tackifier axis is active; otherwise near the linear-dilution prediction
hypotheses.falsified_if: an acrylic-only composition reaches the low-drift regime without any minor tackifier
hypotheses.supported_if: low drift is observed only for compositions with a non-zero minor tackifier fraction

claim_boundary: These hypotheses are formulation-level rheological mechanisms. None of them asserts a molecularly resolved reaction pathway, and no chain-level characterization is implied or required by their adjudication.
